walkthroughs.body_html:
Pilgrimage = a sacred journey.

Jerusalem — sites of Jesus' life, death, and resurrection.
Lourdes (France, 1858) — Mary appeared to St Bernadette; many seek healing.
Walsingham (England) — medieval Marian shrine.
Iona (Scotland) — early Celtic Christianity, now ecumenical.
Taizé (France) — ecumenical community of brothers, attracts young people for prayer and song.

Jesus' Great Commission (Matthew 28:19-20): 'Go and make disciples of all nations'.

Mission includes telling others about Jesus (evangelism), but also living out love — building schools, hospitals, and challenging injustice.

Modern missionaries serve worldwide, often in education, healthcare, and development.

CAFOD (founded 1962) is the Catholic Church of England & Wales' overseas development agency — working in 40+ countries on poverty, climate, and emergencies.

Christian Aid (1945) is sponsored by 40+ British/Irish churches — disaster relief, fair trade, advocacy.

Both reflect Jesus' parable of the Sheep and Goats (Matthew 25): 'whatever you did for the least of these, you did for me.'

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Christians believe in three different gods.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

mcqs.q: What is the Eightfold Path in Buddhism?
options: The Eightfold Path is the same as the Four Noble Truths.

The practical path to ending suffering: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration — grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
The Eightfold Path is eight gods Buddhists must please.
